name: Clarithromycin
route_note: Oral tablets (immediate- or extended-release) or suspension twice or once daily; IV in some countries.
targets: 23S rRNA of the 50S ribosomal subunit (nascent peptide exit tunnel)

discovery.note: Methylation of the 6-hydroxyl group of erythromycin prevents acid-catalysed degradation, improving oral absorption and tolerability.

tagline: Acid-stable macrolide central to H. pylori eradication and MAC treatment
summary: Clarithromycin is a semi-synthetic macrolide developed by Taisho in Japan and marketed by Abbott. It is more acid-stable and better tolerated than erythromycin, and is widely used for respiratory infections, Helicobacter pylori eradication and Mycobacterium avium complex disease.
mechanism: Clarithromycin binds 23S rRNA in the 50S ribosomal exit tunnel and blocks protein elongation; its 14-hydroxy metabolite is also active, particularly against H. influenzae.

It is a strong mechanism-based inhibitor of CYP3A4 and an inhibitor of P-glycoprotein, producing many clinically significant drug interactions. Point mutations in 23S rRNA (A2143G, A2142G) underlie H. pylori clarithromycin resistance.
uses: Helicobacter pylori eradication (with amoxicillin or metronidazole and a proton pump inhibitor)
Mycobacterium avium complex treatment and prophylaxis

history.title: H. pylori indication
history.detail: Clarithromycin-based triple therapy becomes a standard for H. pylori eradication.

history.title: Generics
history.detail: Generic clarithromycin enters the US market.

history.title: Rising H. pylori resistance
history.detail: WHO lists clarithromycin-resistant H. pylori as a high-priority pathogen.

history.title: Cardiac mortality warning
history.detail: The FDA advises caution in patients with heart disease after the CLARICOR trial showed increased long-term mortality.

serious: QT prolongation and torsades de pointes
Serious interactions (e.g. colchicine toxicity, statin myopathy, hypotension with calcium-channel blockers)
Possible increased long-term cardiac mortality in coronary heart disease

facts: Co-administration of clarithromycin with colchicine has been linked to fatal colchicine toxicity.

references.title: FDA Drug Safety Communication on clarithromycin in heart disease (2018)
